articles.title: Mets players are delusional with their whiny complaints about fans cheering Pete Alonso's 300th HR
articles.summary: The New York Mets got swept at home by the Baltimore Orioles in what was an emotional three days for the fans at Citi Field as they welcomed back Pete Alonso...
articles.body:
The New York Mets got swept at home by the Baltimore Orioles in what was an emotional three days for the fans at Citi Field as they welcomed back Pete Alonso , who left the team in free agency this past offseason.

It was evident from the jump just how beloved Alonso is in Mets territory, and it reached a point where Mets fans were cheering him on even though he hit a game-tying home run in the ninth inning of their contest on Tuesday in a game they lost in extra innings, 7-5.

This long ball was the 300th home run of Alonso's career, and considering that he hit the first 264 dingers of his big-league career with the Mets during his seven-season stint with the team, it's understandable as to why fans reacted the way they did. Alonso did cost the Mets the game, but the fanbase's love for him is so strong that they didn't even care.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This struck a chord with some Mets players, who couldn't believe what they were seeing. Sean Manaea , who started for New York on Tuesday, even said that he has never seen anything like it throughout his time in the big leagues. It can be jarring for some players to see their own fans turn against them.

However, the Mets players have to know the entire context of this situation . Rooting for Alonso, and by extension, the Orioles, doesn't necessarily mean that they are rooting against the home team.

Make no mistake about it, Alonso is going to receive cheers from the Citi Field crowd no matter what. But if the Mets were in the hunt for a postseason spot, the reaction to his game-tying home run may not have been as warm. However, New York is not in the playoff race, and one loss doesn't really matter in the grand scheme of things, at least from the fans' perspective.

The Mets fanbase is simply expressing its disappointment with the front office for letting Alonso walk in the first place. They had a few opportunities to sign Alonso to a big deal. In 2025, they reached a compromise, with the 30-year-old first baseman signing a two-year, $54 million contract with a player option for 2026.

The slugging first baseman ended up having a solid 2025 campaign, putting up 38 home runs and 126 runs batted in as they barely missed the postseason. And then in 2026, Alonso, now in his 30s, opted out and was looking for the first huge long-term contract of his career, and the Mets hesitated .

This paved the way for the Orioles to sign him to a five-year, $155 million contract. All along, New York simply did not give Alonso that kind of financial respect, perhaps out of their worry that he wouldn't age gracefully. In 2023, they reportedly offered him a seven-year extension worth a total of $158 million, which goes to show how much they tried to penny-pinch with him.

Making matters worse for the Mets is that they used their budget this offseason to sign Bo Bichette to a three-year, $126 million contract (AAV of $42 million). Bichette is only 28, and he is playing a position of greater defensive importance (third base).

Even then, Bichette has underperformed in his first season in New York (16 home runs, 74 runs batted in, 1.7 fWAR). Meanwhile, Alonso keeps on producing, as he now has 37 home runs and 102 RBIs this year and he already has his best fWAR total since his rookie campaign (4.1).

Again, the greatest panacea to all of this is to win baseball games. That's what the Mets players should keep in mind so they can ease the heartbreak fans feel whenever they see a beloved former player continue to tear it up for another team.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels responds to Terry McLaurin's lack of targets
articles.summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels on Terry McLaurin's lack of targets.
articles.body:
In the Washington Commanders ' season-opening loss to the Philadelphia Eagles , one stat stood out above all others. Wide receiver Terry McLaurin caught just two passes for 14 yards. His first catch didn't come until the fourth quarter, and he had all four targets.

Remember when David Blough was promoted to offensive coordinator; he promised to give McLaurin 10 targets per game. So, what happened?

It's not as simple as it seems. Quarterback Jayden Daniels was under intense pressure from start to finish. Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was more aggressive than normal, pressuring Daniels on 50% of his 38 dropbacks. Remarkably, Daniels was sacked only once, but even when he bought time to work through his progressions, there was often no one open. This was especially true in the first half.

Philadelphia has arguably one of the NFL's best secondaries, and while Daniels and Blough finally got the offense going in the fourth quarter, the Eagles were determined not to let McLaurin beat them. Fangio often used a safety to bracket McLaurin. Philadelphia cornerbacks Tariq Woolen and Quinyon Mitchell played well, too, but they had some help.

What did Daniels think of McLaurin's lack of targets?

The quarterback understands how important it is to get the ball to McLaurin, but he also won't force the issue because he has other talented weapons.

"I think we just have answers for that, and you try to predict what you could see," Daniels said when asked how the Commanders would handle extra attention on McLaurin.

"You're not gonna get every answer to the test right, but you try to have predictions of, like, this could happen, and obviously Philly did a great job with their game plan of taking Terry away and forcing other guys to make plays, which they did. And when those opportunities present itself for Terry to make plays, we gotta make them at the end of the day. I gotta give him a good ball, he gotta catch it, a lot has to go on to successfully have a play. But moving forward, man, we just have answers for that, and not gonna force-feed Terry the ball, but still go through my reads, but when those opportunities present itself for Terry to go make plays, I know he'll make them."

That's a very mature response from Daniels. That's leadership. And there will be headlines out there that will not give you the entire quote. Daniels wasn't saying it with any slight towards McLaurin. You want your quarterback, especially a young quarterback, to go through his progressions and find the open man. McLaurin is not a diva. He's a team-first guy and understands this better than anyone.

Sometimes, you just have to tip your hat to the other team. The Eagles made it a point not to allow McLaurin to beat them. It worked. Fortunately for the Commanders, they now have Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams on the roster to help McLaurin.

articles.title: 49ers news: Christian McCaffrey gets 100% real about head-turning rookie
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey is accustomed to carrying a massive workload, but Week 1 delivered a surprising twist to start the...
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers star running back Christian McCaffrey is accustomed to carrying a massive workload, but Week 1 delivered a surprising twist to start the season. During San Francisco 's dominant 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams , rookie running back Kaelon Black turned heads by taking on a featured role in his official NFL debut.

While fans expected McCaffrey to hog nearly all the backfield snaps, Black surprisingly led the team in carries. According to the box score, the rookie out-carried McCaffrey 14 to 10, turning those touches into 65 rushing yards alongside one catch for five yards. Meanwhile, McCaffrey remained sharp and efficient, racking up 68 rushing yards on his 10 carries while adding five receptions for 20 yards in the passing game.

Rather than feeling threatened by the unexpected backfield split, McCaffrey offered glowing praise for the young rusher. Speaking after the game, the All-Pro superstar kept it 100% real about Black's work ethic, intelligence, and rapid progression.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Yeah, I mean that's the standard. Bobby T emphasizes being a complete back, being able to run it, catch, block, and he came in and since Day 1 he's been on his P's and Q's, and so good to where you can trust him with doing anything," McCaffrey said, shouting out running backs coach Bobby Turner.

Earning trust in head coach Kyle Shanahan's complex offensive system is no easy task, especially for a rookie entering his first pro game. Yet, Black stepped up immediately, proving he can handle blitz pickups, pass protection, and tough interior yards.

Establishing a reliable secondary option in Black is fantastic news for San Francisco. Lightening McCaffrey's heavy weekly burden helps keep the superstar healthy for a deep postseason run while giving the 49ers a relentless one-two punch. If Black keeps building on this impressive debut, San Francisco's offense will be nearly impossible to slow down.

articles.title: The Outlook - Week 2 (DET-BUF, MIN-CHI, CAR-ATL, PHI-TEN)
articles.summary: The Outlook is The Huddle's new matchups column. Kevin Tompkins will break down every fantasy-relevant player from each team every week.
articles.body:
We are through one week of the NFL season, and it makes sense to want to take everything at face value since it's the only true data point that we have so far about this season. While there ARE things that we can take from last week's games, we have a lot to learn about players, teams, their tendencies and a lot more. We're not going to overreact about every single thing that happened in Week 1, but we can take a measured approach while understanding that priors we held before the season have changed, can change and will likely change.

"The Outlook" will give you details, stats, angles, recommendations and everything else you need to know to help you make your fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team playing will be profiled in this article. We want everybody reading this to bring home championships in your fantasy leagues! This week is the first step!

I am incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season and hope you all enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) and tag me in a post to ask me any lineup questions you have, and I will do my best to get them answered for you.

Let's get into it for Thursday night and through the multiple blocks of this article, this Sunday/Monday full slate of games!

(All game/implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Tuesday afternoon for DET/BUF and Tuesday night for CAR/ATL, MIN/CHI and PHI/TEN)

Detroit Lions at Buffalo Bills — 8:15 PM ET

Implied Point Total: Bills 29, Lions 24.5

Goff was 26-of-39 for 206 yards and two touchdowns, leading an extremely condensed Lions offense to a win over the New Orleans Saints in overtime in Week 1. How condensed? Only three wide receivers and eight offensive players even took a snap. If you had just looked at the box score after the fact, you would never know that it was a 7-0 score at halftime. Even though the Lions ended up scoring 31 points, it was really Jahmyr Gibbs that did most of the damage rather than Goff, who still threw two touchdowns to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Goff was QB17 on the week, but the upcoming Bills defense did just allow 31 points to the Houston Texans, so maybe some upside here on Thursday night?

Fantasy Advice: For Thursday night against the Bills, Goff is definitely in play as a low-end QB1 for Buffalo's first game at the new Highmark Stadium.

Somehow, 186 total yards and two touchdowns wasn't good enough for overall RB1 or RB2 on the week! Nonetheless, a Detroit backfield minus David Montgomery rode Gibbs to the tune of 34 touches. It's pretty clear who the Lions want to be the engine of their offense. Backup Sione Vaki is the handcuff here, as he touched the ball three times.

Fantasy Advice: You don't need me to tell you to start Gibbs. He's in your lineup if he's active.

St. Brown continued his assault on opposing defenses in Week 1, where he logged 14 targets, catching 10 of them for 67 yards. In typical ARSB style, they were at a 5.2-yard aDOT, but who are we to complain? St. Brown is one of the most bankable receivers in fantasy, and no opponent changes that.

Fantasy Advice: I don't think you don't need me to tell you to start St. Brown in Week 2. Lock him in this week against the Bills.

Williams was plenty involved and ran an equal 95% route participation with St. Brown in Week 1. He was their downfield threat, posting a 14.2-yard aDOT, but only caught 4-of-9 targets for 45 yards and JUST missed a touchdown as well early in Week 1, as he was down at the 1-yard line before Gibbs plunged in for the score. No other Detroit pass-catcher had more than a 5.7-yard aDOT (LaPorta), so the downfield role was clearly his, and he didn't have to fight any other ancillary pass-catchers for those particular targets given how concentrated the personnel is for the Lions. The Bills gave up four completions of 20+ yards in their win against the Houston Texans in Week 1, so perhaps that could be the avenue to exploit the Bills in Week 2?

Fantasy Advice: Williams is a solid low-end WR2. He might seem like your classic boom-or-bust profile. HOWEVER, there's much more volume in store for Williams, given how condensed the target tree is in Detroit.

It wasn't a super interesting day for LaPorta on the stat sheet, but as we've been harping on, it's a condensed offense. Considering only 2-of-36 targets went to a player that wasn't St. Brown, Williams, Gibbs or LaPorta, that's something you love to see. Better days are ahead for LaPorta in this offense.

Fantasy Advice: LaPorta is still a firm low-end TE1 given the offense he's in and his placement within it.

Allen was awesome in Week 1 against what we all thought was a brutal matchup in the Houston Texans' defense. Two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and 334 yards passing; Allen could do no wrong. Sporting the best air yards/att. (12.8 yards) of all quarterbacks in Week 1, he's using the entire field. There's no scenario where you're not starting anybody else over Allen in a given week.

Fantasy Advice: To repeat the last sentence from above: There's no scenario where you're not starting anybody else over Allen in a given week.

In Week 1, the Bills were a little less pass-curious than I think anybody, with that point being driven home more emphatically in a game where both the Bills and Texans scored 30+ points apiece. With two touchdowns on the ground by Allen and a lot of the work through the air later in the game, Cook was present and accounted for but didn't factor too much into the outcome in the third and fourth quarters — outside of catching a couple of his passes then. Cook will have his weeks, but it just wasn't in the cards for Buffalo's season opener.

Fantasy Advice: Keep Cook locked in as your fantasy RB1, as touchdown variance should shift into Cook's favor sooner rather than later.

Is it time for me to ALREADY get my face pushed into the dirt for Moore? Moore led the Bills in targets (seven) and put up a 5-100-1 line on 81% route participation. His touchdown catch probably should have been stopped by somebody, with Texans S Reed Blankenship diving to tip it but ultimately missing and letting Moore go untouched for the final 20 yards to the end zone. That said, Moore took a little more than a quarter of Allen's targets, which is a nice baseline for fantasy production. I'm still slightly skeptical, though, if Buffalo will be passing like this going forward. For Moore's fantasy managers, at least for one week, it was a great sign.

Fantasy Advice: Against the Lions in Week 2, Moore is a solid, low-end WR2, where you're hoping his Week 1 establishes a floor of how much Allen is willing to look his way.

Shakir put up a 4-50-0 line on five targets but saw a couple of downfield looks in addition to his typical line-of-scrimmage targets that have become his signature. He had a target inside the 2 that could have been an easy touchdown but was tipped away and then had another red-zone target in the middle of the fourth quarter as well. Despite running just 63% routes in Week 1, Shakir was schemed up and is the CLEAR WR2 here behind Moore, but one that has solid opportunity each week.

Fantasy Advice: More of a flex play against the Lions in Week 2, but Shakir tends to punch up a bit with his fantasy value, especially in PPR formats.

I am VERY interested in Kincaid moving forward if this is how he's going to be utilized. Sure, he was a 69% route participation (which would have been a season-high last season) against the Texans in Week 1, but he made his looks count with a 5-130 line on six targets. Kincaid was 50% in the slot and 29% out wide in his alignments in Week 1, so getting Kincaid in space and letting him navigate is what we've wanted from him for YEARS.

Considering Kincaid ran the second-most routes on the team after Moore, I'm hoping this utilization sticks because this is how you get to be a top fantasy tight end. We know the offense can support a clear second target and the Bills are going to score a LOT. Kincaid is one of my favorite storylines to follow through the season for Week 1. If you like having fun, Kincaid is most definitely FUN.

Fantasy Advice: The Lions allowed 14 targets, seven receptions, 87 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 to Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant last week. With that in mind, we're locking in Kincaid as a mid-range TE1 and I don't think that is overdoing it.

articles.title: Ex-Colorado athletics employee admitted to misusing Nike funds year before arrest
articles.summary: Ex-Colorado athletics employee admitted to misusing Nike funds at the school several months before his hiring as CFO of USA Swimming
articles.body:
The former University of Colorado athletics department employee who is facing theft and embezzlement charges in Boulder admitted to misusing Nike funds at the school four months before his hiring as the chief financial officer of USA Swimming in December 2025 , according to an internal university audit report obtained by USA TODAY Sports.

The former employee, Cory Randall Hilliard, 54, is facing three criminal counts related to his administration of the university's Nike Elite program, which provides athletic department employees with funds to purchase Nike merchandise.

"I did it. I admit it," Hilliard told the university's audit department on July 30, 2025, according to the internal audit report.

The audit report was dated Aug. 7, 2025. Hilliard left his job at the university the same month, according to his LinkedIn account. He later was hired as the CFO of USA Swimming in December 2025. He then resigned from USA Swimming after his arrest on these charges in August 2026 , one year after the audit report.

Hilliard is accused of overspending his Nike gear allotment by $9,500 from fiscal year 2022 through the fiscal year ending in June 2025. Any admission to the university's audit department is not the same as pleading guilty in court, which he has not done. He is due to be arraigned in Boulder in October, where he is expected to enter a plea then. His attorney declined comment when reached by USA TODAY Sports.

What happened with these Nike funds at Colorado?

The university's internal report noted how each full-time athletics department employee at Colorado is allotted a certain amount of funds to spend on Nike gear in an online account. This employment perk is part of the university's sponsorship contract with Nike and included an allotment of $621 to $625 annually for employees like Hilliard from 2022-25.

Hilliard served as administrator of this Nike program and could adjust his allocation for the Nike Elite account at any time "without anyone else knowing," according to the report. He overspent his allotment every year from 2022 to 2025, including by $6,011 in 2025 and $2,304 in 2024, the report stated. The report said Hilliard's actions resulted in the loss of $9,501.50, "which could have been used for CU sports teams."

"When questioned if he spent over his allotted $625, he said he did, but it was to purchase Christmas gifts, such as bags and luggage, for the staff within the CU Department of Athletics," the report said. "When IA (internal audit staff) informed Hilliard that the orders for Nike items purchased appeared to be mostly for the men's items in the same size, either large or extra-large, and the men's pants with a size 36-32, Hilliard admitted that he had purchased those items for himself. Hilliard said he could not put a percentage on the total number of items he purchased for himself versus the items he purchased for the staff. Hilliard said he did not have permission to exceed his allotted amount of $625."

University audit report states employee was 'remorseful'

The report noted that from Aug. 21, 2024 to June 27, 2025, Hilliard made 59 orders through his Nike Elite account valued at $6,636 wholesale, all of which were sent to his home address except one. That's $6,011 more than his allotted amount of $625 for fiscal 2025.

"When asked why he overspent his allotted amount, Hilliard said he did so because he had access to the excess Nike Elite funds, and it was an error and a misjudgment by him," the report stated. "Hilliard then said, 'I did it. I admit it.' Hilliard appeared to be remorseful for his actions and told IA that he would be willing to be taxed on the funds over his allotted amount."

The internal audit investigation happened after then-Colorado athletic director Rick George notified the audit department about possible misconduct involving Hilliard in July 2025. At the time, Hilliard had worked at the university for nearly two decades and helped run the athletics department budget.

University police conducted its own independent investigation, which led to criminal charges in August 2026 for theft, embezzlement of public property and first-degree official misconduct.

USA Swimming's hiring history and role in this

It's not clear why USA Swimming didn't know about the internal audit dated nearly four months before his hiring was announced by the organization in December 2025. After his arrest in August 2026, a spokeswoman for USA Swimming said Hilliard was immediately placed on leave without access to any company data or financial controls. The spokeswoman said the organization was conducting an investigation. He resigned the next day.

The spokeswoman told USA TODAY Sports Sept. 14 that there was "nothing new" to report on the case.

Hilliard's hiring at USA Swimming came the same year that the organization had a separate hiring issue with its CEO. The organization announced in February 2025 that Delaware athletic director Chrissi Rawak had been hired for that job. But then Rawak withdrew from it less than 10 days later when the organization learned of a complaint against her at the U.S. Center for SafeSport .

USA Swimming is the national governing body for competitive swimming in the U.S. The organization said then the issue with Rawak was not disclosed to the organization during its "rigorous vetting process" of her.

University of Colorado's history with Nike

Colorado has had a contract with Nike since 1995 and discovered the misappropriated funds during a review of its deal with the company, according to the audit report. That deal was worth $4.75 million in product allotment in fiscal 2025, $90,000 of which was allocated for the Nike Elite program.

The school signed a new five-year deal with Nike in September 2025. Colorado's relationship with the company also played a role in getting head football coach Deion Sanders to return to the Nike fold in 2023 after years of estrangement .

Follow reporter Brent Schrotenboer @Schrotenboer . Email: bschrotenb@usatoday.com

ONE Championship has added a high-profile contest to the ONE Fight Night 48 on Prime Video lineup, pitting two hungry fighters against each other in an atomweight Muay Thai battle that could reshape their promotional trajectories.

Hong Kong's Yu Yau Pui will face the United Kingdom's Marie McManamon at the show, which airs live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, October 2.

Yu's path into Muay Thai began at age 18 as a way to stay fit. The Hong Konger eventually took her first official fight at 22 and never looked back.

She made her ONE Championship debut through the ONE Friday Fights circuit in 2023, reeling off five consecutive victories to earn a US$100,000 contract and a spot on the promotion's global roster.

The 33-year-old made an instant impact in her main roster debut, defeating former ISKA Kickboxing World Champion and WBC Muay Thai World Champion Lara Fernandez in 2024. Since that high point, however, the aggressive striker has hit a rough patch, winning just once in her last four outings.

Five months after knocking out Anna "Supergirl" Jaroonsak and retiring the phenom in Muay Thai action, Yu made the switch to kickboxing and fell to former K-1 Champion Kana "Krusher Queen" Morimoto in a competitive three-round battle this past August. Now holding a professional record of 29-5, Yu looks to rediscover the form that once made her one of the division's biggest threats.

Standing across from her will be McManamon, a 36-year-old representative of the Knowlesy Academy in London, where she trains alongside reigning ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan Haggerty and strawweight phenom Freddie Haggerty .

Widely regarded as one of the United Kingdom's leading Muay Thai strikers, McManamon dominated the domestic scene before making her high-profile ONE Championship debut in 2025, challenging Allycia Hellen Rodrigues for the ONE Women's Atomweight Muay Thai World Title.

The Brit came up short via fourth-round TKO in that outing, and months later, she fell to two-time WBC Muay Thai World Champion Selina "Teep Queen" Flores by unanimous decision.

Now, McManamon looks to re-ignite her ONE Championship career against a fellow veteran who is also motivated to earn a statement victory at ONE Fight Night 48 on Prime Video.

articles.title: Why Barenaked Ladies are singing Canadian national anthem in NFL first
articles.summary: The Bills' new stadium will open with a unique performance from the Barenaked Ladies.
articles.body:
Josh Allen is the main attraction as the Bills open their new stadium on Thursday night, but he isn't the only form of entertainment on hand for the Buffalo faithful.

While OneRepublic will be performing at halftime for the crowd, fans will hear a performance of the Canadian national anthem from rock band Barenaked Ladies.

The Canadian band once threw out the first pitch at a Blue Jays game north of the border, but they are headed just south of the border to help ring in $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium as the Bills host the Lions .

Here's what you need to know about the band and their performance.

Why Barenaked Ladies are singing Canadian national anthem

For the first time, the Bills will play "O Canada" before their home game despite the NFL not having any Canadian teams. That's something the NHL's Buffalo Sabres, who are also owned by Terry Pegula, already do regardless of whether a Canadian team is playing.

Buffalo sits just across the Niagara River from Canada, so the franchise has devoted itself to building a Canadian fan base over the years. Those efforts included games in Toronto during the late 2000s and early 2010s.

With tensions palpable between the U.S. and Canada due to trade disputes, the Bills appear to be extending an olive branch to their neighbors to the north (and west) as they open their new stadium.

So, why the Barenaked Ladies? The band is Canadian, after all, hailing from the Toronto suburbs, and they are one of the top Canadian bands to break through in the United States as well, giving some crossover appeal with a predominantly American audience watching at home.

Here's more to know about the Barenaked Ladies.

The Barenaked Ladies are an alternative rockband that was formed by Ed Robertson and Steven Page in 1988. Robertson remains the band's lead singer.

The band gained popularity in Canada in the early-to-mid 1990s and started to develop an American audience in the late 1990s. Barenaked Ladies' 1998 album "Stunt" featured hit single "One Week," which remains the band's most recognizable song.

As for their name, it came about while Robertson and Page attended a Bob Dylan concert in 1988, Page told the Los Angeles Times in 1992.

"We sat there and talked about all these fake bands we'd like to be in, and started coming up with dumb names for them. I don't know which of us said 'Barenaked Ladies,' but we laughed our heads off," Page said . "It's something we'd say when we were 9 or 10 years old, a phrase we'd forgotten, so it was charming when it popped back up."

When it came time to form a band, the name was brought up again and stuck. True to their name, Barenaked Ladies regularly incorporates humor into their songs and performances.

Despite developing an American audience, the Barenaked Ladies remain popular in Canada and were inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame in 2018. The band is still active, having released a new song earlier this year.

The Barenaked Ladies were formed in Scarborough, Ontario, Canada, a northwest suburb of Toronto. Both Robertson and Page are originally from Scarborough, and three of the four current members are from Scarborough; all are Canadian.

The Barenaked Ladies' most popular song remains "One Week," which reached No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1998. Despite being released 28 years ago, it has been streamed on Spotify over four times more than any other song by the band.

"If I had $1,000,000," released in 1992, is also one of the band's most memorable hits, incorporating humor into the lyrics, while 2000 single "Pinch Me" was nominated for a Grammy Award.

2013 single "Odds Are" stands as one of Barenaked Ladies' most popular modern songs, but they might be best known by some as the singers of the "Big Bang Theory" theme song that plays at the start of episodes.

articles.title: Pau Echaniz: "En los entrenamientos voy creando"
articles.standfirst: El piragüista de aguas bravas, medallista en París al que le han robado el bronce y del que no hay noticias, destaca también con la costura
articles.summary: El piragüista de aguas bravas, medallista en París al que le han robado el bronce y del que no hay noticias, destaca también con la costura
articles.body: Para un apasionado de la moda, ganar una medalla olímpica en un periodo en el que las dos grandes capitales de las tendencias acogieron los Juegos, París -los de verano en 2024- y Milán, los de invierno del 26, de forma consecutiva, fue un capricho de los dioses. El piragüista Pau Echaniz, de la elegante San Sebastián, fue bronce en las aguas bravas de Vaires sur-Marne. Es un deportista singular, el virtuosismo que demostró con la pala para conseguir una medalla que le han robado y aún no ha recuperado, lo replica luego con los patrones y las máquinas de coser. Acaba de ser tercero también en el programa de Televisión Española Maestros de la Costura Celebrity 2, que ganó Beatriz Luengo por delante de Silvia Marty. “Fueron 10 semanas, me lo pasé que flipas”, reconoce. Tiene grandes sueños y grandes ideas en las pasarelas con la firma Pau Etxaniz. Pregunta. ¿Cuántas horas dedica a la piragua y cuántas al diseño? Respuesta. Hay que distinguir entre el invierno y el verano. En invierno no competimos y cuándo estoy en Donosti (San Sebastián), hago preparación física de 9 a 12 y por las tardes, después de comer, en un trastero que he acondicionado como taller, coso. Lo cierto es que en verano estoy casi siempre fuera de Donosti y ahí no tengo tiempo para ponerme delante de la máquina. De hecho, desde abril, he estado en casa dos semanas. P. ¿Por qué empezó a coser? R. Porque tenía que estudiar algo. Y me encantó desde el inicio. P. ¿Qué le frustra más? ¿Un mal entrenamiento o un día en el que no avanza nada con la aguja? R. Es parecido. Muchas veces, cualquiera de ellos no sale como quieres. No será la primera vez que coso algo del reves por tercera vez. Entonces es cuando hay que tener esa mente fría, aparcar tus emociones y tirar hacia adelante. Es cuando te dices, voy a intentar hacerlo sin pensar. Las frustraciones son bastante parecidas. P. Ha confesado que el deporte de alto rendimiento puede volverse “tóxico” y que la moda es su vía de escape. ¿La moda le protege del piragüismo, o hay días en que es al revés? R. Lo que me ha ayudado la moda es a desconectar de los entrenamientos. También si una competición no sale bien, la costura me ayudaba a evadirme. En el deporte de alto rendimiento es vital desconectar. Y también me ha pasado al revés. Muchas veces tengo cosas en la cabeza, ideas que me entran cuando estoy entrenando, sobre todo si son series o trabajo aeróbico. Entonces creo y luego intento trasladarlo a la máquina de coser. P. Balenciaga es su gran referente. Presentó su primera colección en su museo de Getaria. ¿Qué es lo que más le obsesiona de su forma de trabajar el patronaje? R. Es el maestro de todos los que aman la moda. Fue el que cambió la historia, la forma de ver muchas cosas que parecían imposibles. Siendo de Getaria y teniendo en cuenta que sus primeras tiendas las abrió en Donosti, los que somos de allí lo adoramos. Es como Dios para nosotros. Es un maestro de la perfección. Es capaz de crear algo y repetirlo un millón de veces. Puede parecer sencillo a veces, pero es lo más dífícil de hacer. Lo ves y dices: ‘esto no tiene mucho misterio’. Pero ves el patrón y te rompe la cabeza. Para nosotros es lo más difícil. También pasa en la piragua. Hacerlo sencillo, es lo más difícil. P. Usted mezcla patchwork, volúmenes y corsés masculinos. ¿Qué quiere decir con esa estética que rompe tanto con el estereotipo de deportista como con el de diseñador convencional? R. Me gusta experimentar. Y eso he hecho hasta ahora. He podido vender cosas o hacer cosas de encargo. Ahora estoy empezando con mi proyecto de marca y ya quiero hacer algo más serio. Me gustaría entrar en un mundo con algo que me guste, que me inspire. ¿Romper estereotipos? Yo lo veo cool. El romper estereotipos es lo normal. Crear es mi pasión. P. Se lleva la máquina de coser a algunas competiciones. ¿Diseñaba o cosía en plena concentración olímpica? R. No, siempre llevo en la mochila mi cuaderno, mis lápices o apunto en el móvil. Tengo momentos que dibujo. Lo de coser físicamente en grandes competiciones, no. Pero me las imagino. Siempre intento hacer algo porque luego, cuando llego a casa, tengo cosas que hacer y está guay avanzar. P. ¿Si pudiese trasladarse a una época, cuál elegiría? R. Ni idea. No me iria lejos. A 2009 ó 2005. Fueron años muy potentes. O ahora mismo. Todas las épocas tienen sus cosas guays. Estamos en un punto muy guay en la moda. Las marcas tienen que renovarse siempre en la epoca que sean y aparecen cosas nuevas. P. Picasso dijo aquello de que las musas te pillen trabajando R. Y es verdad. A mí me funciona. Muchas veces no tengo claro qué hacer y simplemente empiezo y me voy acercando a lo que quiero hacer. Piensas: ‘No me va a salir’, pero se trata de arrancar e ir probando P. San Sebastián siempre asociada a la moda, ¿se identifica con esto o su estilo es radicalmente distinto? R. Es una ciudad un poco clásica, no tan moderna como podría ser Barcelona. A mí lo clásico no me echa para atrás, pero me gustan cosas más modernas. Cosas que ni yo pueda entender. Huyo de lo clasico de toda la vida. Es un poco mi espíritu de ser libre. P. ¿En qué pasarela le gustaría ver desfilar sus modelos? R. Es como preguntar si quieres ser campeón olímpico. Tengo mucho camino por delante, acabo de empezar y voy poco a poco. Me gustaría mi ciudad. O la 080 de Barcelona, que suele tener marcas muy potentes.l

articles.title: Manu Bhaker's Asian Games medal preparations hit by 50-km commute: India shooting coach unhappy with arrangements
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: A senior coach travelling with India's 30-member shooting contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has expressed disappointment over the arrangemen.
articles.body: A senior coach travelling with India's 30-member shooting contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has expressed disappointment over the arrangements in Japan, saying the long travel time between the team's hotel and the shooting range has become a major issue ahead of the competition.The coach, as quoted by news agency PTI, said he arrived in Japan with high expectations but felt the arrangements had not matched what he expected from the host country. According to him, the Indian shooters have been accommodated around 50 km away from the training and competition venue and are staying in different hotels.For a contingent that includes some of India's top medal contenders, such as double Olympic bronze medallist Manu Bhaker and multiple Asian Games medallist Esha Singh, the daily commute has meant early starts and long hours on the road to keep up with training schedules.“This (transportation) is a real problem. But what can we do about it? I didn’t see any hotels in the vicinity of the shooting range. If there were, we would have reached early. They gave us accommodation at a place which was far, so now what can we do about it?” the coach, who was not named, said as quoted by PTI.He said the issue had been communicated to the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI), though he had not spoken to federation officials about it in recent days.“I presume the federation (NRAI) would have told them (Asian Games organisers). I haven’t spoken to the federation about it, but we had informed the federation about this issue and this discussion had been going on," he said.The coach also pointed out that long travel times are not unusual in shooting because ranges are often located away from cities and residential areas.“Having said that, I would also like to highlight that the ranges are very far away from main habitation. In China (2022 Hangzhou Asian Games) also, it used to take one hour to reach the range. So it has now become a part of shooting,” he said.“But having said all that, Japan being Japan, I am a bit disappointed with the arrangements. It could have been better.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early 2026 Vezina Rankings for NHL Best Goalie
articles.summary: As we head into the 2026-2027 season, pondering who might win the Vezina Trophy as the NHLs best goaltender can lead you down into a rabbit hole filled with stats, past winners, and recent hopeful heirs to the throne.
articles.body:
As we head into the 2026-2027 season, pondering who might win the Vezina Trophy as the NHLs best goaltender can lead you down into a rabbit hole filled with stats, past winners, and recent hopeful heirs to the throne.

As finicky and volatile as the goalie position can be, there are a few who are still active that have been consistent enough to win the Vezina multiple times (Sergei Bobrovsky, Andrei Vasilevskiy and Connor Hellebuyck) and one of the latter two have won it in five of the past eight seasons.

Handicapping the goalies who will be in the running to win it this year takes equal amounts of tea leaf-reading and faith as well as trusting that some things refuse to change. The goalies expected to be at the front of the pack will have its familiar faces, but team success can bring some unexpected candidates to the forefront. We'll give you our thoughts about who we see being in the mix for the award right now as training camp opens across the league.

The three-time Vezina winner and 2025 MVP was suspended by the Winnipeg Jets for not showing up at training camp. He wants a trade and he's willing to stay home despite having a contract to make it happen.

He's coming off his worst season as a pro (.895 save percentage) and yet still had his greatest personal accomplishment helping Team USA win the gold medal at the Olympics where he played brilliant, big-time hockey. Goalies not getting time in at training camp can struggle and although Hellebuyck is one of the best goalies we've seen in recent times, if/when he's traded, adjusting to a new team can take time.

We're not saying he's got zero chance to win it this year, but we'd like to see who he plays for (Buffalo? New Jersey? Carolina?) and just when he starts playing for them before making him one of the favorites to win another Vezina.

Throughout last season, the Hurricanes were able to steady themselves and take control thanks to the play of Brandon Bussi. This season, Bussi is set to take charge of Carolina's net now that Frederik Andersen headed to Edmonton and with the defending Stanley Cup champions playing dominant, winning hockey that results in great numbers for their goalies, Bussi will be in the conversation.

What we're most eager to see is how Bussi handles an increased workload. He had an .895 save percentage with two shutouts in 39 games last year and went 31-6-2. Doing all of that as a rookie goes a long way to ensuring people will pay attention moving forward.

Vezina's usually get handed out looking beyond the win-loss record, but now that the Hurricanes have everyone's attention as champions and the respect Bussi earned during the regular season and again in the playoffs for locking down the Cup going 3-1 to close out the Final, he'll have a lot of eyes on him to see what he does to follow up a great debut season.

Nothing puts a goalie on the map like playing brilliantly in the playoffs and nothing ups the ante like doing all of that with the Montréal Canadiens. The way Jakub Dobeš did all of that in leading the Habs to the Eastern Conference Final last season set the bar for him to be a modern legend.

Dobeš's play last season in seizing the starting job for the Canadiens and then winning two Games 7 against Tampa Bay and Buffalo has fans in Montréal at a fever pitch to see how far he can take them this season and beyond. In 43 games last season, he went 29-10-4 with a .901 save percentage in what was his official rookie season.

Although the Canadiens have another young top prospect in Jacob Fowler coming into his own as well, it is Dobeš who won hearts last season with his acrobatic play, big saves in big moments, and of course, playoff success. If he can build on what he did in a sizable way, that kind of play under that kind of pressure will put the spotlight on him for the Vezina.

Although the New York Rangers had a brutal season last year, one of the few players you couldn't blame for that was Igor Shesterkin.

Shesterkin was tied for third in the league in save percentage (.912) with Vezina winner Andrei Vasilevskiy and Washington's Logan Thompson. The Rangers distinct lack of success and Shesterkin having but one shutout didn't help set him aside to make his case as a great performer on a losing team. He did finish seventh in Vezina voting last year with two second-place votes (NHL general managers vote on the award).

He won the Vezina in 2022 after a brilliant season which he posted a .935 save percentage with six shutouts and a 2.07 goals-against average. Being one of a handful of former winners currently playing, he's in rare company, but if he can have a similar season with a few more shutouts and more team success and perhaps a return to the playoffs, he's a more than viable contender for a second Vezina.

7. Scott Wedgewood/Mackenzie Blackwood, Colorado Avalanche

When it comes to the Avalanche, you expect to see Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar lead the way for them. What we didn't expect to see last season was Scott Wedgewood to become a Vezina contender. It can also be said we didn't expect to see Wedgewood and goalie tandem mate Mackenzie Blackwood to swap in and out so often in the playoffs, too.

The team in front of Wedgewood and Blackwood determines a lot of their win/loss success, but Wedgewood led the league with a .921 save percentage last season as well as his 2.02 goals-against average with four shutouts. Blackwood's .904 save percentage with three shutouts made him one of the better goalies in the league as well which puts both of them in a position to contend for the Vezina this season should either of them take control of the net.

That's not to say that a split crease can prevent one of the goalies from winning the Vezina. Linus Ullmark won his in Boston years ago while splitting time with Jeremy Swayman nearly evenly. Wedgewood's numbers last season should've put him in better contention for the Vezina (he was fifth in voting), but he wasn't able to knock off Andrei Vasilevskiy. A repeat performance this season might be the kind of thing that puts him in the driver's seat, if Blackwood doesn't beat him to it.

Quietly, one of the best goalies around the league the past few seasons has been Logan Thompson. From his time in Vegas to his past two seasons in Washington, all Thompson has done is stop a lot of shots very often.

For his career, Thompson has a .912 save percentage and in 58 games with the Capitals last season after taking the No. 1 job from Charlie Lindgren, he posted a .912 save percentage with four shutouts. The Caps finished just shy of the playoffs and any hope Thompson had of winning the Vezina was outshined by others with great seasons of their own.

That said, consistency goes a long way in goaltending and Thompson has it so long as he's healthy, and he has been with Washington. With the improvements Washington has made in the offseason adding Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, getting the Capitals back to the playoffs to give Alex Ovechkin one more run at a Stanley Cup might be the equation that leads to a Vezina for Thompson.

When the Bruins parted ways with Linus Ullmark and made Jeremy Swayman their No. 1 goalie, we all wondered how that would work out given the increased workload. Although a prolonged contract negotiation got in the way of things a couple seasons ago, Swayman proved last season what he's capable of doing without distractions.

Swayman finished third in Vezina voting after he put up a .907 save percentage with two shutouts and led the Bruins to a 100-point season and a return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs. He went 31-18-4 in 55 games and although the Bruins were knocked out in the first round by Buffalo in six games, reestablishing himself as one of the best goalies in the league allowed Boston to get their swagger back as a team.

If Swayman can pick up where he left off last season and lead the Bruins back to the playoffs in an even tougher Atlantic Division, it'll be difficult to look past his efforts in making that happen. He's a known quantity and now that he owns the net in Boston, that role comes with a lot of respect attached to it.

4. Filip Gustavsson/Jesper Wallstedt, Minnesota Wild

The Wild were one of the best teams in the NHL a year ago and two of the biggest reasons why came from goalies Filip Gustavsson and Jesper Wallstedt.

While Gustavsson was the No. 1 and played brilliantly on his own with a .903 save percentage and four shutouts in 50 games (49 starts), it was rookie Wallstedt who announced his arrival with a .915 save percentage and four shutouts in 35 games (33 starts). There are worse problems to have than two goalies playing outstanding hockey, but there's only one net to play at a time and the Wild are already paying Gustavsson starter money to do it.

But a new season means there's a clean slate and should Wallstedt improve upon what he did last season, it'll put pressure on Gustavsson to up his game as well. A split net doesn't necessarily hurt either goalie's chances of winning a Vezina but should one or the other take the net and run with it while playing great, it would be hard to look past them for the award.

Last season wasn't a great one for Jake Oettinger. Sure, he was part of the gold medal winning U.S. Olympic team, but his play with the Dallas Stars was hot and cold. Even though backup Casey DeSmith played great to support him, Oettinger could've done better and he'd even tell you as much.

What that tells us is that Oettinger is due for a big season and a return to elite form. He had an .899 save percentage in 54 games with four shutouts. That save percentage mark was the lowest of his career and it's hard to imagine that he would have two straight difficult seasons, mostly because that's yet to happen in his career. He has a career save percentage of .910 and a regression to the mean would be a huge comeback year for the 27-year-old.

Despite Oettinger having a tough year, the Stars were one of the best teams in the NHL a year ago. Picture that effort with improved play from the starter and perhaps an extended run in the playoffs and you've got the recipe for a goalie who's destined to win the Vezina at some point in his career.

It's a shame the New York Islanders dealt with so many injuries and inconsistent play last season because it buried a great story of Ilya Sorokin returning to dominant form in goal.

Sorokin led the NHL in shutouts with seven and while his .906 save percentage in 55 games was the lowest mark of his career, given all the issues the Isles had, his play made it look a lot better than it was. He went 29-24-2 last season and finished second in Vezina voting behind fellow countryman Andrei Vasilevskiy despite all of that.

Although Sorokin is yet to win a Vezina, he's done nothing but play outstanding hockey year in and year out for the Islanders. Now with new coach Pete DeBoer in place on Long Island and his history of success, another great season from Sorokin could see him lead the Islanders back to the playoffs and finally take home the hardware.

1. Andrei Vasilevskiy, Tampa Bay Lightning

To be the man, you've got to beat the man, and Andrei Vasilevskiy did that last season by knocking Connor Hellebuyck off the pedestal for the Vezina. For years, Vasilevskiy has been one of the most respected and feared goalies in the league. Winning back-to-back Stanley Cups will help make that happen, but playing big in every big situation will help seal that reputation.

Last season, Vasilevskiy had a .911 save percentage, down from the .921 from the year before when he finished second to Hellebuyck for the Vezina. But he helped reestablish the Lightning as one of the best teams in the NHL and went 39-15-4 in 58 games. His win total was best in the league among goalies. It was his ninth straight season with 30-or-more wins and even though he had just two shutouts, the body of work was impossible to ignore as he cruised to win his second Vezina Trophy.

With good health and an outstanding team around him, there's no reason to think Vasilevskiy can't run it back and win it again this year. If he has another great season statistically with how tough the Atlantic Division is, he might wind up in the MVP discussion as well.

articles.title: What’s the Asian Games accommodation crisis, and where will athletes stay?
articles.summary: In a cost-cutting move, Japan decided against setting up a dedicated athletes’ village but now faces a backlash.
articles.body:
The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games get under way this weekend under the shadow of a housing crisis that has organisers scrambling to placate athletes and officials from participating nations.

The tournament has been mired in complaints over housing options for athletes travelling to Japan, after the host nation decided not to build a dedicated Games village for the 17,000 competitors and officials.

To cut costs this year, organisers are relying on a cruise ship, temporary wooden cabins and hotels, but this temporary accommodation has met with criticism in the days leading up to the continental competition.

On Monday, South Korean officials slammed beds in shipping container-style huts as the “worst-ever”, as the South Korean basketball chief said the beds were too short to stretch out in.

Why are the Asian Games facing an accommodation crisis?

The official housing committee said the issue arose because they expected 15,000 athletes and officials, but numbers increased as new sports were added.

This year’s Games will feature several newcomers, including mixed martial arts, padel and surfing, as well as virtual taekwondo and teqball, which ‌‌combines aspects of football and table tennis.

Ahead of the Games’ opening, chief organiser Hideaki Omura said efforts are being made to ensure athletes are comfortable.

“If there are different opinions, then we will respond to them appropriately,” Omura, who also serves as governor of Aichi prefecture, told the AFP news agency.

“At this point, while we are responding to individual opinions, we have been improving everything as issues arise, and we will continue to respond that way.”

He added that a committee of former athletes, including Olympians, gave a favourable assessment of the plans for the huts built this year.

“We explained everything to them and had them take a look around, and they said it looked functional and good,” he said.

Where will the Asian Games athletes stay?

Alternative housing options range from a cruise liner and wooden containers to hotel rooms.

On Tuesday, the Italian cruise ship, Costa Serena, which will host 4,000 athletes and officials, arrived in Nagoya.

The shipping container-style huts in the dock area of Japan’s biggest port will host 2,000 other athletes and officials.

On Thursday, Japan’s deputy Chef de Mission Hisashi Mizutori told a news conference that athletes have been going through entry procedures since the cruise ship village opened a day earlier.

“There have been cases where coaches, team officials and athletes have been assigned to the same room. There are also situations where room assignments were made purely based on the numbers, such as assigning five twin rooms for a group of five men and five women,” Mizutori said.

“While the numbers match on paper, practically it creates challenging situations such as men and women being assigned together, coaches being assigned with athletes, or trainers who need to accommodate a lot of medical equipment being assigned together.”

He added that the Japanese Olympic Committee (JOC) had also anticipated accommodation “challenges” and secured hotels in the city as a backup.

“We are currently working to coordinate and negotiate adjustments wherever possible. For cases where that proves too difficult, we are considering using the backup accommodations that Team Japan prepared in advance as alternatives.”

Why are participating nations and athletes complaining about the accommodation?

Jung Jae-yong, vice president of the Korea Basketball Association (KBA), slammed the cabins hosting the men’s basketball team .

“Athletes who are over two metres tall cannot even stretch their legs out on the beds. It’s unreasonable.”

Jung also accused the organisers of failing to respond to South Korea’s concerns about the housing options.

“The organisers have still not said anything,” he said, adding: “We are very concerned and discussing extensively with the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee what to do about this.”

Player Byeon Jun-hyeong, from the basketball team, posted a video on social media showing a leaking sink and a soaked floor in his hut.

Philippine Olympic Committee president Abraham Tolentino also said that while all his athletes had been given a room, “some officials, like coaches, were moved to different hotels and Airbnb”.

Why will cricketers get the best accommodation at the Asian Games?

Head of Japan’s cricket association, Naoki Alex Miyaji, said in early September that cricket would get better accommodation than other sports .

According to Miyaji, the cricket tournament is being run by the Asian Games organising committee in collaboration with the Asian Cricket Council.

He said that the two bodies had been discussing accommodation options “for a long time”.

“The participating teams in cricket are being offered hotel accommodation,” Miyaji said.

“Many other sports are being accommodated in much more limited facilities, such as a cruise ship or container hotels.”

What other issues have hit the Asian Games?

While the opening ceremony has yet to take place, several events such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon have already begun.

On Thursday, Tropical Storm Dujuan was located off Japan’s Pacific coast as of 03:00 GMT and heading northwest towards central Japan, where Nagoya is located.

Last week, torrential rains hit Nagoya and the surrounding areas, forcing schools to close and suspending train services. Several hundred athletes were also forced to leave their accommodation .

Kosei Inoue, Japan’s chef de mission for the Games and a senior executive board member of the JOC, said at a news conference on Thursday that some competitions have already experienced “delays or postponements, and there is also a possibility that a typhoon could approach on September 21”.

“Under these circumstances, we are holding thorough meetings within the JOC to ensure that we are fully prepared and capable of responding appropriately to these situations.”

articles.title: Roman Reigns' In-Ring WWE Legacy Is Getting a Major 2026 Rewrite
articles.summary: Fair or not, Roman Reigns has always been a performer whose on-screen presence and written character were considered far greater than his in-ring work.
articles.body:
Fair or not, Roman Reigns has always been a performer whose on-screen presence and written character were considered far greater than his in-ring work.

When he had great matches, it was always with the help of his proverbial dance partner. His greatest in-ring moments included some magical angles, like Seth Rollins' unforgettable cash-in at WrestleMania 31 or Cody Rhodes finishing his story nine years later, after five of the most electric moments in wrestling history.

There has always been a bigger moment or a greater excuse than Reigns simply being fairly great at what he does. Here in 2026, however, that in-ring legacy in WWE is getting a major rewrite.

Reigns was the big dog before the aforementioned 2024 match with Rhodes. There was no question that The Tribal Chief was the guy before The American Nightmare returned to the company in 2022 and began a steady climb to the top of the professional wrestling mountain, which culminated in his win over the OTC on wrestling's grandest stage.

The most popular high school jock, the apple of everyone's eye, had been knocked off his perch by a new QB1. He bided his time, watched the new face of the company guide it through the next year, and by the time 2026 arrived, he set out to reclaim his mantle.

Not just as the Tribal Chief, leader of The Bloodline, and possessor of a godlike aura, but in an area of his performance that had long been overlooked: between the ropes.

The Royal Rumble win catapulted him to championship contention, and it was from there that the second-generation star and future Hall of Famer began his greatest stretch of ring work.

Reigns is at a point in his career where he could easily have enjoyed a main event run simply based on the connection he has with the audience, his proven track record as a main event attraction, and that aforementioned otherworldly aura.

Instead, he refocused himself and has turned in some of the best in-ring performances of his career.

The match at WrestleMania 42 against CM Punk, where he won the World Heavyweight Championship, was an instant classic and one of the best matches that historic event has ever seen.

The follow-up against Jacob Fatu at Backlash has probably been lost among the other extraordinary matches he has had this year, but it was a damn good, physical war that set up months of storytelling, including what is still playing out on TV every week.

The rematch was not quite as good, but still pretty damn excellent, and the match against Seth Rollins at SummerSlam was an epic encounter that played on nearly 15 years of backstory.

His most recent banger, a successful title defense against Penta in Mexico City that saw him go far out of his way to put over the former Intercontinental Champion as a legitimate threat to his title, was just a step below the WrestleMania 42 match and easily the best match WWE has produced on free TV this year.

What can his superb run of in-ring performances be attributed to besides his dogged determination to silence the critics? The answer is far simpler than one might think.

One of the issues surrounding his first, historic run as the Tribal Chief and world champion was the creative team's reliance on interference from his Bloodline teammates. It fit the story of a gaslighting, egotistical champion who did not realize how important his minions were to him in preserving his spot at the top of the company. It did become rather repetitive after *checks notes* three years , however.

Again, as if motivated to shut up those who nitpicked and found fault with his previous performances, Reigns has wrestled matches by himself, proving he does not need his family around to fight his battles for him.

Without all of the overbooked nonsense and incessant run-ins, Reigns has been able to prove to the wrestling world that he can work as well as anyone, wrestling extraordinary main events with any opponent booked across from him.

Punk, Rollins, Fatu, and Penta are all great workers, but they all have different styles. Reigns has been the common denominator, so hiding behind the old "look who he's working with" argument carries no weight.

The effort to tell the story of a seasoned champion who can achieve victory without any help is the biggest difference between this run and last, and more importantly, between "very good" and "great" matches.

While WWE has undoubtedly been tempted to run the Usos or Fatu out to the ring to interrupt a match and advance the Bloodline Saga, it has resisted the urge and Reigns has paid that decision off by leaving fans more than satisfied with the content of his in-ring work.

Already one of the industry's biggest draws, with his name on some of the highest-revenue shows in company history, Reigns has begun improving the one area of his legacy that still attracts skeptics and doubters. The result has been a staggering array of stellar marquee matches and suddenly silent haters.

articles.title: Vikings QB Kyler Murray working towards playing in Week 2
articles.summary: Kyler Murray was limited in practice on Wednesday ahead of Week 2.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings all offseason discussed their quarterback position over and over again. Just like we did. Sadly, the position was not settled, as Week 1 had one more wrinkle.

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray went down with a concussion after a tough hit in the first quarter. Murray was sliding and was sandwiched between two defenders in a hit that got social media going. Murray stiffened up after the hit, signaling a concussion.

The team quickly confirmed a concussion and ruled him out for the remainder of the game.

Fast forward to prep for Week 2 against the Chicago Bears , Murray was in the practice report on Wednesday and was listed as limited. He was seen with a helmet and pads on, and a classic no-contact jersey, which makes it seem promising that he could play in Week 2.

Now, could they be slow in bringing him back after seeing how Carson Wentz played in his place? Perhaps. The team remains committed to Murray as the starter, and concussions are serious, so how he progresses through Thursday and into Friday will be important to watch.

articles.title: ‘Where we had imagined bridges, a wall has gone up’ – RC Lens’s general manager on the reasons behind Dino Toppmöller’s departure
articles.summary: The news of the split between RC Lens and their manager Dino Toppmöller will undoubtedly remain one of the most memorable stories of the early stages of the...
articles.body:
The news of the split between RC Lens and their manager Dino Toppmöller will undoubtedly remain one of the most memorable stories of the early stages of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 season. Not necessarily because the German, who has since been replaced by his assistant Yannick Cahuzac, had made a particularly strong impression, but mainly because he ultimately did not have time to do so. Three months, six matches, one trophy, and the story of a revival had already come to an end.

And whilst the reasons for this split had remained rather vague until then – based on journalistic speculation – Lens's managing director, Benjamin Parrot, took it upon himself on Thursday to explain them to the press. And he did so quite simply. For in his view, the partnership between the northern club and Toppmöller quite simply "didn't work out" .

"Even before the Trophée des Champions, we sensed that there were two camps within the coaching staff – one from Lens and one from abroad," the club official explained. "Where we had hoped to build bridges, a wall had gone up. We put a whole host of measures in place to bring everyone closer together: a statement from Jean-Louis (Leca, the sporting director), meetings… but this lack of connection was having an impact on the team."

"We therefore had to act responsibly and make a decision. It may have been perceived as interference in sporting matters, but no, it was a management decision aimed at bringing everyone closer together. The coach did not accept this decision. We had to take responsibility."

Standing alongside Parrot, Jean-Louis Leca for his part made a point of paying tribute to Toppmöller as "an extraordinary man, a good coach" , recalling that "we were convinced back in June that this was the right choice, that we could bring something extra to the table. It didn't work out."

articles.title: The 'F1 of athletics'? Athlos set for London debut
articles.summary: Keely Hodgkinson and Georgia Hunter Bell will be among the stars in action when the all-female track meet Athlos makes its London debut on Friday, live on th...
articles.body:
The all-female track meet Athlos will make its London debut live on the BBC on Friday - and its founder hopes the competition can become the "Formula 1 of track and field".

Created by Alexis Ohanian, Reddit co-founder and husband of tennis' 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams, Athlos was held in New York for its first two editions in 2024 and 2025.

It was due to expand to a two-day event in 2026, however this year's New York meet scheduled for 2 October was cancelled.

Ohanian said that decision was taken after listening to athlete concerns at the end of a long season, adding that from 2027 Athlos "will move to be aligned with the global athletics calendar".

Many of the world's top athletes competed for a new global title and record prize money at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship last week.

In addition to chasing a top prize of $65,000 (£48,500) in each event, and an Athlos crown designed by Tiffany & Co, athletes will be offered equity in the league - the idea being that they will be rewarded if it is successful.

Great Britain's Keely Hodgkinson and Georgia Hunter Bell, American sprinters Gabby Thomas and Sha'Carri Richardson, and Dominican 400m runner Marileidy Paulino are among the star names competing.

The event will take place at the StoneX Stadium in Barnet, home of rugby union side Saracens, on Friday, 18 September, with coverage on iPlayer, the Red Button and the BBC Sport website and app from 19:00 BST.

"I've long been very obsessed with this 'F1 for track and field' analogy. We come to expect the fastest cars in the world to tour the greatest global cities, and for people to come out and watch and celebrate this excellence," Ohanian told BBC Sport.

"I envision Athlos to be a version of that and, as we grow this league, I'd love to add more cities and make Athlos truly global.

"Whatever we do, we're going to do it with our athletes as partners - but our ambition is big. I don't see any reason why Athlos can't be a mainstay of the sporting calendar."

'We get a share in what we're helping to build'

The financial difficulties encountered by Michael Johnson's Grand Slam Track in its inaugural season last year have been well-documented, but Ohanian says he is determined to close the "historic gap" which has existed between "the economics of women's track and field and the excellence of the talent".

Athlos is owned entirely by Ohanian's venture capital firm Seven Seven Six, which has assets of $900m (£670m) - but athletes will receive a stake so they may also benefit if the competition succeeds.

"The cash compensates their participation and success, and the equity recognises what we're building together. If we get this right, it should properly place these amazing athletes on the same level as they are every four years during the Olympics," said Ohanian.

"This equity is a way for us to have a real partnership. These are the athletes who are the first movers, the ones who are taking a leap and helping us get this started."

Ohanian prioritised athlete input from the outset, reaching out to individuals such as Olympic 200m champion Thomas via social media long before Athlos' inaugural season in 2024.

Speaking to BBC Sport in May, against the backdrop of protest plans by the world's leading tennis players over prize money at the French Open, Thomas, a Harvard graduate with dreams of running her own hospital once her time in the sport ends, said Athlos was sending "a real signal".

"We get a share in what we're helping to build and that's really rare in this sport," said Thomas.

"How can we fail as a league when we have the athletes as partners and helping to build it? We know the sport better than anyone."

Thomas added: "When a young girl watches me race, I want them to see a sport where women are treated with respect and with the economics that we've always deserved, and have something to aspire to.

"The narrative growing up was that you can't run professional track and field, there's nothing in it. I like that we're rewriting that."

'I want to do things that have big impacts'

Seven disciplines will be contested in London - the 100m hurdles, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, mile, and long jump - with six athletes in each event.

Athletes can earn up to $65,000 (£48,500) in each individual event, with $35,000 (£26,000) on offer for second place and decreasing prize money for all six positions.

Olympic 800m champion Hodgkinson was among the winners at the 2025 meet as some of the world's fastest women competed amid a party atmosphere inside a packed Icahn Stadium in New York, with live music and the Tiffany & Co crowns presented by Serena Williams replacing traditional winners' medals.

Following the addition of a London event in 2026, Ohanian's ultimate aim is to create a worldwide, season-long league.

"I'm at a very fortunate place in my career in my life where I don't want to do anything small. I want to do things that have big impacts, that are about legacy," said Ohanian, who bought a 10% stake in Women's Super League football team Chelsea last year.

"We know we're entering into something really ambitious. This is a big moment for us."

Originally published May 2026, updated September 2026.

articles.title: Five random thoughts as the Penguins begin training camp
articles.summary: This is one of those days where I have a few thoughts bouncing around but I am not sure any of them are enough for a full, dedicated article. So you’re getti...
articles.body:
This is one of those days where I have a few thoughts bouncing around but I am not sure any of them are enough for a full, dedicated article. So you're getting a bunch of random thoughts just emptied out of my head for your consumption as the Pittsburgh Penguins open training camp.

1. Does anybody need a strong camp more than Ville Koivunen ?

The most surprising, and some might say shocking, Penguins move of the offseason was actually one of their last moves when they signed Ville Koivune, after just 47 NHL games and only two goals, to an eight-year, $32 million contract.

Given everything that's happened over the past couple of weeks, and especially the past few days in the lead-up to the start of the new CBA, it's starting to make a little more sense, and honestly doesn't look quite as baffling (and while it shocked me, I never quite saw it as THAT baffling and could see the thought process behind it ). Given the buyout rules, where the cap is going in the coming seasons, what player contracts are starting to look like, and all Koivunen needs to do to make it worth it, it's still a relatively low-risk, potentially high-reward deal.

EVEN WITH THAT, there are no good optics in the short-term for him showing up at camp, not earning a spot on the roster, and being sent to the American Hockey League after signing an eight-year deal.

Maybe it's for that reason that he already has a spot "locked" in. And maybe, given the current depth at forward, it wouldn't be the end of the world if he did get sent down at the start (because they do have a lot of good players at forward), but it still wouldn't look great. Sometimes optics stand out more than facts and reality, but that still matters.

Everybody has talked about what a good offseason he has had. His underlying numbers this past season were some of the best on the team. There is reason to like him. But it is time to start turning all of that into tangible results on the scoreboard.

2. The goalies will dictate the season and where it goes

In terms of the forwards and defense, I see this roster looking pretty similar to the one the Penguins were using in 2025-26. The forwards are pretty good, and pretty deep. I don't love the defense, but Erik Karlsson can still be an impact player and I do think there is a chance this current group will defend better than last year's (I like Declan Carlile as a potential under-the-radar steal; Trevor van Riemsdyk is a legitimately good defensive player; I am intrigued by what Kaeden Korczak can do in a potentially bigger role).

But going into the season with two young, still very unproven goalies is a GIGANTIC wild card that could take this thing in any number of directions.

Everybody loves Sergei Murashov 's upside, and he has been great at every level since coming over to North America. But it's still just upside with him at this point, and the AHL isn't the NHL. He's still a young goalie, and young goalies are still completely unpredictable. His ceiling is high. His floor is low. There's a gigantic empty space he could fit in.

Arturs Silovs has had his moments, but consistency has not been his calling card in the NHL.

If these two guys put it all together and show they are ready for the big-time on a full-time basis, I could see a scenario where this team is not only back in the playoffs, but that it's ceiling is a little higher than last year's team and a higher than a lot of people are expecting.

If they are not ready for that? Or if they struggle? You might very well end up in a position to get the top-five pick you are still searching for.

3. Egor Chinakhov and Nicholas Robertson intrigue me more than any other veteran players in camp

I know what Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin are going to do this season.

I have a pretty good idea as to what Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust are going to do.

The fourth line guys are what they are, and I know what they are.

There are a lot of unknowns with the younger players like Ben Kindel , Rutger McGroarty , Ville Koivunen, Bill Zonnon, Harrison Brunicke , Tomas Galvas, and the goalies, but that is the nature of the beast with young players. Some of them will become NHL players. A couple might be really good NHL players. You might get lucky and one becomes an All-Star. Some will be a hit, most will strike out. As smooth Jimmy Apollo once said , "when you're right 52 percent of the time, you're wrong 48 percent of the time."

But Chinakhov and Robertson remain the most intriguing mysteries to me because they have some NHL track record, have shown some ability to be good NHL players, and they have very obvious NHL talents, but they are still very much unknowns.

Chinakhov is oozing with talent and top-line ability, and he really put it all together in the second half of the 2025-26 season after being acquired in the trade from the Columbus Blue Jackets . Was it a real improvement, or just a short-term flash? Can he still take a star turn? If he can, that changes some math for you in the short-term and long-term.

It is a similar question for Robertson, who has some very real NHL skills, and has scored goals at a top-line rate per minute, but has never really had an opportunity to show if that can translate into something more.

I don't think either is out of reach, but neither one is guaranteed to reach those levels. They are not quite as big of a wild-card as the goalies, but they remain wild-cards for what the team's success level and ceiling is.

4. Which veteran is going to get waived?

After last year's training camp we see Ryan Graves and Danton Heinen get waived.

Matt Dumba and Philip Tomasino followed not long after during the season.

Given the forward depth it, where they legitimately have 17 or 18 players that could play on the NHL roster, it seems likely that somebody is going to get waived by the conclusion of camp.

Could it be Filip Hallander ? I thought he was solid before his season got derailed, but where does he fit? Could it be Justin Brazeau ? Hendrix Lapierre fits the mold of the type of player the Penguins have been rolling the dice on , but he's far from a lock.

I suppose a trade is still possible, but I just don't know where that comes from at this point.

This is just a guess. It is just a prediction. But I say he signs a one-year, $8.7 million extension by the end of camp and does this every year from now until his eventual retirement. I do not believe he has any interest in playing elsewhere. I also believe he means it when he says it is all just about how he feels physically.

articles.title: Valakari on Gray departure, being linked with Hibs & Falkirk 'focus'
articles.summary: St Johnstone manager Simo Valakari has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Scottish Premiership visit of Falkirk.  On Hibs head coach David Gray bec...
articles.body:
St Johnstone manager Simo Valakari has been speaking to the media before Saturday's Scottish Premiership visit of Falkirk .

On Hibs head coach David Gray becoming the first Premiership managerial casualty of the season, Valakari says: "He is my colleague and of course I feel for my colleague", adding it shows "the ruthlessness of this business".

When asked about being among the early names linked with the Easter Road job, the Saints boss says when there is a vacancy somewhere, "all the coaches will be thrown in", and his "full focus" is on Saturday's game.

Valakari adds: "My players are doing the good job, my club is doing the good job and that is the only reason as a coach you will be linked."

With his team seventh in the table, with seven points from six games, the Perth manager is not "surprised where we are" because he has "seen these players now for one year, I am very happy with the players we have brought in".

Valakari believes there is a "lot of room for improvement as well".

On Falkirk, the Finn is "very, very impressed with how they play football", saying John McGlynn's side really showed what they can do in their midweek win over Hearts.

Valakari insists Saints are just taking it one game at a time and the midweek results show what can happen when you are off it.
